subject: Climate & Environment
title: From Farm Loss to Fork Waste
description: A 60-second lesson on From Farm Loss to Fork Waste.

hook.text: In sub-Saharan Africa, 40% of food is lost after harvest — before it ever reaches a market.

buildup.text: Poor roads, no refrigeration, and few storage facilities mean crops rot in the field.

discovery.text: Simple solutions like solar dryers and metal grain silos can cut post-harvest loss by half.

twist.text: In wealthy countries, the waste shifts to the consumer. Americans throw out 40% of their food.

climax.text: The problem is different at each stage but the effect is the same: resources wasted, people hungry.

punchline.text: Hunger and waste exist side by side. That's the real scandal.

quiz.question: Where does most food loss occur in sub-Saharan Africa?

details.summary: Food is lost at every stage from farm to fork. In developing countries, poor storage, unreliable transport, and lack of cold chains cause most losses at the production stage. In wealthy countries, supermarket rejection of imperfect produce and consumer behavior drive waste at the end of the chain.
details.whyItMatters: Addressing food waste requires different solutions at different points in the supply chain. Targeting the biggest loss points in each context maximizes impact and resource savings.
takeaways: Developing nations lose food mainly during harvest and storage
Wealthy nations waste food at retail and consumer stages
Cold chain infrastructure reduces post-harvest loss dramatically

faq.question: What is a cold chain?
faq.answer: A cold chain is an unbroken series of refrigerated storage and transport links that keeps perishable food at safe temperatures from harvest to consumer. In many developing countries, lack of cold chain infrastructure causes up to 40 percent of food to spoil before it reaches market.

faq.question: Why do supermarkets reject so much produce?
faq.answer: Retailers enforce strict cosmetic standards: odd shapes, small sizes, or minor blemishes lead to rejection even though the food is perfectly safe and nutritious. This drives enormous waste at the farm level. The ugly food movement works to change these norms.
